title: Continuous flow optimizer and kernel negotiator
creator: Aisha Rahman
description: Context: Persistent tail latency spikes on multi-tenant prefills despite kernel-level heuristics. Current admission only looks at per-request latency deadline and a coarse kernel cost table; it doesn't negotiate kernel choices when batch shape evolves mid-prefill or when attention KV reuse suggests different kernel paths. This ticket implements a two-part runtime improvement: (1) Continuous Flow Optimizer (CFO) — an admission/batch-shaping controller that issues lightweight flow-tokens and dynamic shaping signals to smooth token arrival variance and prefer cooperative batch shapes; (2) Kernel Negotiator — an in-runtime component that performs incremental kernel selection during the prefill->decode transition, using a short negotiation heatmap between admitted requests to pick kernels that minimize aggregate latency while respecting per-request SLOs.
goals: Reduce p99 end-to-end prefill+decode latency by at least 15% on mixed short/long workloads
Reduce p99 tail latency variance (p99.9 - p99) by 30% for prioritized customer routes
Avoid regressions in throughput (<= 5% throughput degradation) vs current baseline
Provide trace-level visibility into negotiation decisions for rollout and debugging
success_metrics: p99 end-to-end latency improvement >= 15% on synthetic mixed workload (daily perf test)
p99.9 tail variance reduction >= 30% on production shadowing for 1 week
No more than 5% increase in token-cost per request on average across runs
Enablement of kernel-negotiation debug traces without >1% additional CPU overhead
constraints: Must be implementable without kernel binary changes (user-space runtime only)
Feature must be toggleable per-customer and per-route via runtime flags
Memory footprint increase <= 20MB per serving process
Negotiation latency budget for kernel decision must be <0.5ms extra on critical path
design_summary: CFO introduces a token-credit mechanism: arriving requests receive flow-tokens that carry lightweight metadata (expected sequence length, attention-window-hints). The admission controller converts tokens into shaped micro-batches using a smoothing window and a small decay factor; micro-batches are fed to Kernel Negotiator. Kernel Negotiator computes a short-lived heatmap of candidate kernel costs (estimated using a cost model that considers current GPU occupancy, KV cache hit stats, and attention sparsity hints) and runs a fast combinatorial heuristic to select a kernel configuration per micro-batch. For transitions where prefill and decode kernels differ, negotiator favors decode kernels with lower incremental tail risk for requests with tight deadlines, while allowing longer-deadline requests to use more throughput-efficient kernels. Decisions are recorded to tracing and emitted to the Console rollout dashboard. We also add a lightweight backoff policy: when negotiated cost exceeds a threshold or contention is detected, CFO defers non-critical requests for up to 10ms to avoid tail amplification.
acceptance_criteria: CFO and Kernel Negotiator can be toggled on/off per route via feature flag and remote config
End-to-end tests simulate mixed short/long prompt mixes and assert p99 improvement >= 15%
Shadow rollout on 20% traffic for 72h with no SLO breaches; monitoring dashboards present negotiation traces
A GitHub PR with unit and integration tests merged; performance regression <5% throughput impact verified in CI perf job
implementation_notes: Create new runtime module: runtime/negotiator with C++ core + Rust orchestration shim
Extend admission API to attach flow-token metadata; preserve backwards compatibility if token absent
Implement negotiation cost model: lightweight estimator based on kernel bench table + current occupancy probe
Add smoothing window implementation to existing continuous-batcher with tunable decay and max-hold parameters
Expose negotiation decision events via trace span + compact protobuf event to control plane
Feature-flag gate and per-route config in Console; add rollout toggle in runtime-config service
Bench microbench for negotiation overhead (aim <0.5ms) and memory overhead (<20MB)
Write integration test that injects attention-sparsity hints and asserts negotiator picks the lower-latency kernel
testing_plan: Unit tests for flow-token encoding/decoding and smoothing math
Synthetic end-to-end perf harness using mixed prompt length generator (50% short <40 tokens, 30% mid 100-300, 20% long >800)
Canary shadow run: 20% traffic for 72h, monitor p50/p95/p99/p99.9 and tail variance
Chaos test: introduce artificial kernel slowdowns to validate backoff and deferral behavior
A/B test with and without negotiation enabled on dedicated cluster to validate cost delta
monitoring_and_metrics: tail-variance metric: p99.9 - p99 and long-tail incidents per hour
resource metrics: GPU occupancy, mem-bandwidth utilization while negotiation active
alert: >10 SLO breaches in 1h in canary => auto-disable feature for route
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Negotiation adds CPU overhead causing contention. Mitigation: strict CPU budget and fast-path bypass when CPU high; ability to disable negotiation globally.
Risk: Incorrect cost model leads to poor kernel choices. Mitigation: conservative defaults, continuous shadowing and per-route learning weights; ability to revert to static kernel table.
Risk: Tracing volume increases. Mitigation: sample negotiation traces (1%) and provide compact aggregated counters for Console.
Risk: Customer routes with strict pinned kernels may not benefit. Mitigation: per-route opt-out + explicit pinning respected by negotiator
rollout_plan: 1) Integration + unit tests merged behind feature flag
2) Internal perf runs and benchmarks on staging cluster; tune smoothing decay and negotiation threshold
3) Shadow-run on low-risk production routes for 72h (20% traffic), gather metrics
4) Canary enable on non-critical routes (5% traffic) with O11 alerts for tail regressions
5) Gradual ramp by 10% increments with monitoring signoff; full enable only after 2 weeks of stable metrics
